title: Pushing an ideal factor down through a separated etale morphism of algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a representable surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Let $T$ be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, let $W$ be an algebraic space over $S$ and let $\varphi:W\to T$ be a quasi-compact separated etale morphism, and let $U\subseteq T$ be a quasi-compact open subspace [def-weil-open-immersion]. Morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties]; in particular separated means that the relative diagonal is a representable closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], etale means the chart test of that node for etale scheme morphisms [def-weil-etale-morphism], and quasi-compact means that $W\times_TZ$ is quasi-compact for every affine scheme $Z$ mapping to $T$. Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ be a quasi-coherent ideal on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], of finite type, meaning etale locally generated by finitely many sections. Assume $\mathcal I|_{W\times_TU}=\mathcal O_{W\times_TU}$. Then there exist finite-type quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ and $\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal O_W$ such that $$\mathcal J|_U=\mathcal O_U,\qquad \operatorname{im}(\varphi^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_W)=\mathcal I\mathcal I'.$$ Tensor pullback is as in [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and the product ideal is the image of multiplication $\mathcal I\otimes_{\mathcal O_W}\mathcal I'\to\mathcal O_W$. Fibre products are sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. No surjectivity of $\varphi$, Noetherian hypothesis, or density hypothesis on $U$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-etale-finite-fp-envelope] to $\varphi$ to obtain $W\xrightarrow{j}Y\xrightarrow{\pi}T$ with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion and $\pi$ finite of finite presentation. Finite morphisms are integral on scheme tests; hence [lem-sfb-space-integral-qcqs-permanence] shows that $Y$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and that $\pi$ is affine, quasi-compact and separated. Choose a surjective etale map $T_0\to T$ from a quasi-compact scheme, and a surjective etale map $U_0\to U$ from a quasi-compact scheme. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests], a quasi-compact morphism has quasi-compact pullback over every quasi-compact scheme; so $W\times_TT_0$ and $Y\times_TU_0$ are quasi-compact spaces. They map surjectively and etale (base changes of $T_0\to T$, $U_0\to U$) onto $W$ and $Y_U=Y\times_TU$; composing a quasi-compact scheme atlas of each source with these maps gives quasi-compact scheme atlases, so $W$ and $Y_U$ are quasi-compact. Hence $j(W)\cong W$ and $Y_U$ are quasi-compact opens of $Y$, and so is their union $V=j(W)\cup Y_U$, covered by the disjoint union of the two atlases.

On the overlap $j(W)\cap Y_U$, the ideal transported from $\mathcal I$ equals the unit ideal, by the hypothesis on $W\times_TU$. Therefore it glues with $\mathcal O_{Y_U}$ to an ideal $\mathcal I_1\subseteq\mathcal O_V$. The gluing identifies the ideals as subsheaves of the same structure sheaf on the overlap, so the inclusions glue too. Quasi-coherence and finite type are local and hold on both opens. Apply [lem-sfb-space-finite-type-submodule-extension] to the ambient module $\mathcal O_Y$ and the quasi-compact open $V$ to obtain a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_2\subseteq\mathcal O_Y$ with $\mathcal I_2|_{j(W)}=\mathcal I$ and $\mathcal I_2|_{Y_U}=\mathcal O_{Y_U}$.

Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow Y$ be the closed subspace defined by $\mathcal I_2$, using [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence]. It is of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-closed-structure-finite-presentation]. Set $\tau=\pi i:Z\to T$. Finite presentation of this composite follows from [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition]. It is finite: on an affine scheme test $\operatorname{Spec}A\to T$, write $Y_A=\operatorname{Spec}B$ with $B$ a finite $A$-algebra; the closed subspace $Z_A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(B/K)$, and the images of finite module generators of $B$ generate $B/K$ over $A$. Finally $Z\times_TU$ is empty because its defining ideal on $Y_U$ is the unit ideal.

The structure module $\mathcal O_Z$ has the one-generator, no-relation local presentation. Hence [lem-sfb-space-finite-fp-module-direct-image] makes $F=\tau_*\mathcal O_Z$ a finitely presented quasi-coherent module. Define $\mathcal J=\operatorname{Fit}_0(F)$ using [lem-sfb-space-fitting-ideal-calculus]; it is a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal. The map $\tau$ is affine since finite maps are integral, so [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-base-change] applied to $U\to T$ identifies $F|_U$ with the direct image from the empty space, namely zero. By the rank-zero convention for the zeroth Fitting ideal and its pullback equality, $\mathcal J|_U=\mathcal O_U$.

Write $P=W\times_TY$. The graph $s=(1,j):W\to P$ is open: the open subspace $W\times_Tj(W)\subseteq P$ identifies with $W\times_TW$, and $s$ there is the open diagonal of the separated etale map $\varphi$, by [lem-sfb-space-separated-etale-diagonal-complement]. It is closed in all of $P$: it is the pullback of the closed diagonal $Y\to Y\times_TY$ of $\pi$ along $(j\operatorname{pr}_W,\operatorname{pr}_Y):P\to Y\times_TY$. The latter diagonal is closed because $\pi$ is separated (step 1). Scheme-test definitions of open and closed immersions show that their pullbacks remain such immersions. Thus $s(W)$ is open and closed in $P$.

Pull this open and closed subspace back to $Q=W\times_TZ\subseteq P$. The resulting part is $Z_{\mathcal I}=W\times_YZ$, the closed subspace of $W$ defined by $\mathcal I$, by [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence]. Let $Z\prime$ be its open and closed complement, so $Q=Z_{\mathcal I}\amalg Z\prime$. Both $q:Q\to W$ and $\tau\prime:Z\prime\to W$ are finite of finite presentation. Here are explicit chart checks, using the affine algebra tests and base-change compatibility of [lem-sfb-space-relative-spec-correspondence]: pullback replaces a finite algebra with a tensor algebra, whose finite module generators and finite algebra relations pull back. A clopen component of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is defined by an idempotent $e\in B$; its algebra $B/(e)$ is finite with one additional algebra relation, so retains finite presentation. Therefore [lem-sfb-space-finite-fp-module-direct-image] applies to $\tau\prime$ and makes $N=\tau\prime_*\mathcal O_{Z\prime}$ finitely presented quasi-coherent.

By affine base change for $\tau$, $\varphi^*F\simeq q_*\mathcal O_Q$. The disjoint union of step 6 identifies this module with $(\mathcal O_W/\mathcal I)\oplus N$: on each etale object, sections over a disjoint union are the product of sections on its two components, and a two-factor product of modules is their direct sum. The first summand is the quotient structure module by [lem-sfb-space-closed-ideal-correspondence]. Set $\mathcal I\prime=\operatorname{Fit}_0(N)$, finite type and quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-fitting-ideal-calculus]. On any affine etale chart $\operatorname{Spec}A\to W$, the Fitting ideal of $A/I$ is $I$: the one-generator surjection $A\to A/I$ has kernel $I$, and its maximal kernel-row determinants are precisely the elements of $I$. By [lem-trf-fitting-ideal-direct-sum], $\operatorname{Fit}_0((A/I)\oplus N_A)=I\operatorname{Fit}_0(N_A)$. The chart characterization in [lem-sfb-space-fitting-ideal-calculus] therefore gives $\operatorname{Fit}_0(\varphi^*F)=\mathcal I\mathcal I\prime$ as ideal subsheaves.

The pullback equality of [lem-sfb-space-fitting-ideal-calculus] gives $$\operatorname{im}(\varphi^*\mathcal J\to\mathcal O_W)=\operatorname{Fit}_0(\varphi^*F)=\mathcal I\mathcal I\prime.$$ Together with step 4 this is exactly the required conclusion. All equalities concern image ideals, so none assumes injectivity of tensor pullback of an ideal.
